Maia vs Relevance AI

Choose a ready channel coworker or build an agent workforce.

Relevance AI gives builders a platform for custom agents, tools, and multi-agent workforces. Maia gives teams a coworker already shaped around Slack collaboration.

The short answer

Relevance AI is a platform for building agents, tools, and multi-agent workforces. Builders can configure integrations, triggers, knowledge, models, schedules, escalation, evaluation, and deployment. Maia is a ready Slack coworker product. Its main unit is a channel coworker with instructions, memory, tools, and approvers.

Choose Maia when teams want to adopt a shared coworker through Slack with less agent-building work. Choose Relevance AI when an AI or operations team wants to design a custom workforce and control how agents divide and execute jobs.

A lead handoff example

A marketing channel passes a lead to sales. The inputs include the approved qualification criteria, a handoff message, and a supplied CRM record. The team needs missing questions and a reviewed follow-up, not an invented score.

With Maia, the revenue channel coworker applies the team's criteria and posts discrepancies in the thread. Marketing and sales can resolve conflicting names or dates in one conversation. The sales manager reviews the proposed follow-up before any connected action. The channel retains corrections to its handoff instructions.

With Relevance AI, a builder can create separate research, qualification, and outreach agents, give each its own tools, and combine them into a workforce. Triggers can start work automatically, smart escalations can involve a person, and the platform provides an activity center and higher-plan analytics. This is a strong fit when the company wants a purpose-built agent system rather than one general channel coworker.

Choose Maia when

Choose Maia when the users who own the process configure it through normal Slack work. The shared thread exposes ambiguity so a manager can approve the next step. Different channels keep distinct briefs and access rules without a central builder modeling every branch.

Maia also suits companies that want the collaboration interface provided as part of the product. Verify the required integrations and model options during evaluation.

Choose Relevance AI when

Choose Relevance AI when a builder needs custom agents, tools, triggers, workforces, evaluations, and deployment controls. The platform advertises more than 2,000 app integrations and 1,000 triggers, alongside custom app and API support. Paid plans add scheduling, smart escalations, activity history, shared projects, analytics, and enterprise access controls.

Relevance AI's pricing separates actions from vendor model credits. One action is a tool run and can represent simple or multi-step work. Compare costs with observed tasks because its units do not map directly to Maia credits.

Test builder effort

Implement the same lead handoff in both products. Include conflicting data, a revoked connection, and a follow-up that requires approval. Record how long setup takes, who can change it, how failures surface, and what the end user sees.

For Relevance AI, inspect the workflow, tool logs, evaluation options, and end-user access. For Maia, inspect channel guidance, requester identity, approval, and memory. The right product depends partly on whether agent building is a capability the company wants to own.

Common questions

Does Relevance AI work with Slack?

Relevance AI advertises a broad integration catalog. Confirm the current Slack trigger, action, and end-user experience required for the workflow. A listed integration does not prove a persistent shared Slack coworker.

Can Maia split work across agents?

Yes. Maia can hand part of a job to a subagent, a copy of the same coworker, that reports back in the thread. Its user experience remains centered on the channel coworker rather than a visual multi-agent workforce builder.

Which is better for custom agent teams?

Relevance AI is the clearer fit when builders need to design and evaluate a custom workforce. Maia is the clearer fit when a team wants a managed coworker in Slack and does not want to build the agent platform.
